name: Argythamnia

project_scope.selection_mode: three already-installed canonical species; genus lesson builder
project_scope.source_pool: Master Plant Pool; Genus Study Index

shared_genus_recognition.look_here_first: At a stem node, first check whether the leaf has a petiole. Then measure the entire axillary inflorescence from base to tip and determine whether the raceme itself is unisexual or bisexual. Only after that move to stamens, capsule and seed.
shared_traits: Perennial herbs or low subshrubs in Euphorbiaceae
Simple alternate leaves with malpighiaceous hairs in at least part of the genus
Tiny unisexual flowers arranged in axillary inflorescences
Three-carpellate capsules; seed size and surface are useful confirmation characters
shared_genus_recognition.caution: Low stature, gray-green color and limestone habitat overlap. Do not key these three from habit or hairiness alone.

species_comparison_matrix.Argythamnia aphoroides: 3.7–5 mm; smooth, lightly tuberculate or striate

field_key_training.if: A definite 2–10 mm petiole is present
field_key_training.then: Strongly favor A. humilis; confirm its very short 0.7–0.9 cm raceme.

field_key_training.look: Whole axillary inflorescence beside a ruler
field_key_training.if: Raceme is only about 7–9 mm long

field_key_training.look: Longer raceme, then determine whether the raceme itself contains one sex or both
field_key_training.then: Favor A. aphoroides; confirm 10 stamens and larger 7–9 mm capsule.

field_key_training.look: Longer raceme with both male and female flowers

field_key_training.if: Flowers are absent or the sex arrangement is unclear
field_key_training.then: Use fruit/seed size and surface as the final confirmation; do not force an ID from habit.

overlap_and_cautions: A. aphoroides and A. simulans are both sessile-leaved and can have overlapping raceme lengths; the unisexual-versus-bisexual inflorescence distinction and stamen count are therefore especially important.
A. humilis can be hairy or glabrous. Pubescence does not define the species.
Staminate petal attachment to the androphore is variable in A. simulans and should not be treated as a hard binary.
A. simulans remains learner-approved with unresolved project range status; morphology polish does not change that range label.
Use accepted Argythamnia names in the learner while retaining Ditaxis synonyms for search and cross-reference.

local_lookalike_routing.separate: Check for conspicuous stinging hairs and different raceme/pedicel organization; do not handle without protection.
Examine enlarged pistillate bracts, often toothed/lobed, and inflorescence structure; compare flower morphology rather than leaf hairiness.
Check for stellate or scaly indumentum, gland and inflorescence details; do not assume silvery foliage is Argythamnia.
Find cyathia (cup-like pseudoflowers) instead of the separate conventional staminate/pistillate flowers of Argythamnia.

look_here_first_sequence: 1. Is there a petiole? A. humilis usually has 2–10 mm; the other two are sessile.
2. Measure the raceme. A. humilis is only 0.7–0.9 cm; the others are several centimeters long.
3. On a long raceme, ask whether the inflorescence is unisexual (aphoroides) or bisexual (simulans).
5. In fruit, use capsule and seed size/surface.

visual_lesson.title: Three Argythamnia: measure the leaf stalk, then inspect the flowering raceme
visual_lesson.intro: Photograph the node first. A. humilis has a visible petiole and short axillary raceme; A. aphoroides and A. simulans have essentially stalkless leaves and longer racemes. The last pair requires floral sex and stamen counts, not a broad habit impression.
visual_lesson.teaching_order: leaf attachment → raceme length → unisexual versus bisexual inflorescence → stamen count → capsule

steps.title: 1 · A. humilis: locate the petiole
steps.look_for: The existing voucher shows general plant and leaf position. To measure the 2–10 mm petiole or tiny 0.7–0.9 cm raceme, obtain a separate close-up with ruler.
steps.why_it_matters: Petiole and short raceme distinguish humilis from the two sessile-leaved species.

steps.title: 2 · A. aphoroides: sessile leaves, unisexual racemes
steps.look_for: Leaves essentially without petioles; axillary raceme 3–8 cm. Confirm inflorescence sex and 10 stamens in a dissected male flower.
steps.why_it_matters: The sex of the raceme helps separate it from A. simulans.

steps.title: 3 · A. simulans: sessile leaves, bisexual racemes
steps.look_for: Stalkless leaves and long racemes; inspect both floral sexes on inflorescence and count 7–8 stamens in male flowers.
steps.why_it_matters: Avoid calling it aphoroides from the leaf alone.

steps.title: 4 · Confirm the fruit and male flower
steps.photo_role: matched capsule profile and stamens macro
steps.look_for: Compare verified mature capsules and count real stamens under magnification. Do not infer a count from yellow-green bloom silhouettes.
steps.why_it_matters: The genus can be deceptive without small reproductive structures.

visual_lesson.lookalike_warning: Other small Euphorbiaceae can have inconspicuous flowers and pubescence; confirm Argythamnia with an exact botanical key and specimens rather than appearance alone.

comparison_cards.title: Find the leaf stalk: humilis versus the sessile pair
comparison_cards.look_here_first: Measure the petiole at the leaf node, then the entire axillary flowering raceme.
comparison_cards.caution: Measure actual nodes and intact racemes; a cropped or immature inflorescence is not a reliable length comparison.

comparison_cards.title: Sessile-leaved pair: aphoroides versus simulans
comparison_cards.look_here_first: Inspect multiple complete inflorescences for male and female flowers, then dissect a male flower.
comparison_cards.caution: Raceme lengths overlap; verify flower sex and actual stamen counts on several mature specimens.

comparison_cards.title: Fruiting confirmation across all three
comparison_cards.look_here_first: Measure a mature capsule and seed with a millimeter ruler; inspect capsule hairs and seed surface.
comparison_cards.caution: Fruit size overlaps for aphoroides and simulans; use the floral-sex/stamen key too. Exact fruit macros remain unverified.
